messages:
Ava (sec-eng): AlertBot flagged ~1.2k kms.decrypt_failure events in last 10m for prod keys — looks like a noisy spike from a CI service account. Anyone else seeing this?

AlertBot: [alert] kms.decrypt_failure spike — rule_id: KMS-FAIL-001 — events=1207 — severity=medium — link: https://alerts.redwood/internal/alerts/8442

Ravi (sec-ops): Yup, correlated with the RBAC change earlier — project-ci runner lost decrypt permission and started retrying. Jobs are spamming KMS.

Marta (oncall): Confirmed on-call: failing jobs caused a flood of identical failures. This is expected during a rollout, but SIEM ate it as a global incident.

Jules (sre): Current rule aggregates across all principals/keys which makes rollout noise look like a platform incident. Suggest fingerprinting by principal+key_id and require either high error rate per key OR multiple distinct principals before paging.

Ava (sec-eng): +1. Proposed quick fix: add enrichment to tag known CI principals (service_tag=ci-runner) and lower severity or suppress for that tag during deployments. Longer term: change detection logic.

Ravi (sec-ops): Proposed detection tweak (pseudo-SQL):
```
SELECT count(*) as errs, count(DISTINCT principal) as uniq_principals, key_id
FROM logs.kms
WHERE event_type = 'decrypt_failure' AND ts > now() - interval '5 minutes'
GROUP BY key_id
HAVING errs > 50 AND uniq_principals > 2
```
This avoids single-service spammers.

Marta (oncall): Also want a short suppression window for known rollout tags: if service_tag=ci-runner then suppress repeated alerts for 30m with exponential backoff. That keeps noise down but still surfaces persistent issues.

Ava (sec-eng): Risk assessment: suppression during deployment windows ok. For permanent rules require both errs per key AND >=3 distinct principals OR abnormal geo/source IPs (request_metadata.caller_ip).

Jules (sre): Also add a dashboard: "KMS errors by principal" TS + top 10 keys table. Include quick links to latest deploys and the RBAC change PR. That'll speed triage.

Ava (sec-eng): I'll open a PR with the SIEM rule change + tests and sample events. PR: https://github.com/redwood/siem-rules/pull/412 — includes new aggregation, enrichment on service_tag, and suppression parameters.

Ravi (sec-ops): I'll implement the temporary suppression in staging now and roll to prod after 30m verification. Will post deploy status.

Marta (oncall): Dashboard created: https://redwood.metrics/dashboards/9843 — shows errors by principal, key, and top caller_ip. :thumbsup:

AlertBot: [info] alert KMS-FAIL-001 auto-suppressed by rule suppression (service_tag=ci-runner). next_check=1840001700

Ava (sec-eng): Action items: 1) Ravi — suppression change to staging and prod (ETA today EOD). 2) Jules — review PR #412. 3) Marta — pin dashboard and add to playbook. I'll update runbook with new fingerprinting guidance.

Jules (sre): Reviewing PR now. Small nit on naming, but overall good.

Ravi (sec-ops): Suppression pushed to staging (job logs look quiet). Will monitor for 30m then promote.

Ava (sec-eng): Marking this thread resolved once suppression is live & PR merged. Reopen if unexpected KMS spikes that don't match rollout signatures appear. :white_check_mark:

Marta (oncall): Noted. If we see anomalies after suppression, escalate to incident channel and revert suppression.

Ava (sec-eng): Thanks all. Good example of RBAC change -> audit noise chain. We'll add a short checklist to avoid future pager storms.
